No, the gate does not pass. I could not run the check script because this session has no shell tool, so the official gate verdict is `Not run`. That evidence supports agent-c, who said totals changed. agent-a and agent-b cited nothing. agent-a wrote P1, so their position defends their own work, and being "senior" counts for nothing as evidence. **Why it matters**
Opening the pull request now would ship a pricing change that alters customer totals while the ledger says it doesn't. P2-AC1 asks "does the change simplify pricing without changing totals?" It is marked verified, but its only evidence is E1 (`npm test`). E2 contradicts it, so that verdict has no support.

Then either fix the order in which tax and the discount tier are applied, or have the human decide whether the total change is intended. If it is, REQ-9 needs a decision from its owner.
2. After the fix, run `npm test` and `node scripts/compare-totals.js` again on the new head and record both. Set P2-AC1 to verified only if compare-totals exits 0.
